Use the N–mm–MPa unit system throughout.
Given: L = 1500 mm, G = 25939.8 MPa, T = 1 000 000 N·mm, allowable twist φ_allow = 0.75° over the full length.
Convert φ_allow from degrees to radians using φ_allow_rad = 0.75 × π / 180.
Use the torsion relation φ = TL / (J G) and rearrange to solve for the required polar moment of inertia: J = TL / (φ_allow_rad × G).
Substitute J = π d⁴ / 32 and solve for the minimum solid-shaft diameter: d = (32 J / π)^(1/4).
All quantities are in consistent N–mm–MPa units, so no additional unit conversions are needed beyond the degree-to-radian step.
State the final answer as the minimum diameter d in millimetres, rounded to a practical value (e.g., one decimal place or the nearest standard shaft size if convenient).
Assume the shaft is prismatic (constant circular cross-section), the material is homogeneous and isotropic, and the loading is pure torsion with no axial or transverse shear contributions to the twist.
